text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You have been experiencing headaches and worsening vision for three weeks; to begin our assessment, does the headache occur in the morning or upon waking?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intracranial Mass Lesion (e.g., Brain Tumor).

Based on your age and the three-week history of worsening headaches and vision changes, this suggests increased intracranial pressure or direct optic nerve compression. To confirm this, I need to see the results of your recent neuroimaging and know if your headaches are worse in the morning or with straining. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST TEST: Visual Field Exam.
